Why go: a night in Ang Thong Marine Park

Every day boat leaves Ang Thong by about 15:30. If you stay, you get Koh Wua Talab (Wua Ta Lap), the park headquarters island, almost to yourselves: the beach in the late light, sunset from the viewpoint or the sand between about 18:00 and 18:45 depending on the month, a sky with no town lights, and a second morning in the archipelago before the first boats arrive around 10:00. That quiet window is the whole point of camping here, and something no day tour can offer.

Day one follows the standard speedboat route: the Emerald Lake on Koh Mae Ko (15–20 minutes up steep wooden steps to the lookout over the Thale Nai lagoon), then kayaking, snorkelling and lunch around Koh Wua Talab. When the day boats leave, you stay. Day two is slow: an optional sunrise climb with a torch (sunrise is about 06:00 from May to October and 06:30–06:40 from January to March), breakfast, kayaking and snorkelling in the calm early hours, and a walk to the quieter beach on the west side before the return boat around 15:00. You are back on Koh Samui at 16:00–16:30.

You sleep in a national park tent at the official campground on Koh Wua Talab, the only island in the park with visitor facilities. The tent comes with a sleeping pad, sleeping bag, blanket, pillow and mosquito net. This is simple national-park camping, not glamping: no hot water, electricity until 21:00 and limited Wi-Fi. For a bed and a roof, choose the bungalow version of the same trip for 600 THB more.

Who this tour is for

  • Travellers who want Ang Thong without the crowds, and photographers after sunset and sunrise light over the islands.
  • Couples and friends who are happy with basic camping for one night.
  • Families with older children who enjoy camping. Children aged 3–11 pay the child price and infants up to 2 travel free.
  • Walkers who want to do the Wua Talab viewpoint twice, once in the heat and once at dawn.

Who should choose another tour

  • Want a proper bed, a fan and towels: the overnight bungalow trip.
  • Only have one day: the speedboat day tour or the VIP tour.
  • Need air-conditioning, hot showers or reliable signal: stay on Samui and do a day trip.
  • Pregnant or with back problems: both crossings are by speedboat over open sea; we don't advise it.
  • Travelling 1 November–15 December: the park is closed; the overnight trip restarts on 16 December.

What to bring

  • A torch or head torch (essential for the walk down after sunset and the dawn climb).
  • Insect repellent and a light long-sleeved layer for the evening.
  • A small towel, a change of clothes and basic toiletries.
  • A power bank: electricity on the island runs only until 21:00.
  • Reef-safe sunscreen, a hat and shoes with grip.
  • Cash in Thai baht for the park fee (300 THB per foreign adult, 150 THB per child aged 3–14) and for drinks or anything at the park restaurant not covered by your package.
  • Personal medication and any snacks you can't do without: there are no shops on the island.

Good to know

  • Season: the park is closed every year 1 November–15 December. February to April has the calmest sea and the clearest nights; May to September is good most days; October is wetter. December to February is peak season and campground places are limited, so book early.
  • Weather on day two: the captain decides when it is safe to cross, and in strong wind the return can be delayed, so don't book a flight or ferry for the afternoon of day two. If we cancel before departure for weather, you choose a full refund or a new date.
  • The park restaurant: dinner is served 18:00–19:00 near the visitor centre, and the kitchen closes at 19:00, so don't stay on the viewpoint too long.
  • Park rules: no alcohol is sold in the park, fires are not allowed, swimming in the Emerald Lake is not allowed, and food must be kept away from the monkeys. Take every piece of rubbish back with you.
  • Wildlife: dusky langurs (dusky leaf monkeys) and long-tailed macaques live on Koh Wua Talab. Watch them, don't feed them, and zip your tent.
  • Mobility: the campground is on the beach, but the viewpoint trail is steep with ropes, and the night walk needs a torch and steady feet.
  • Children: children's life jackets are always on board and children wear them at all times on the boat.
  • Drones: need prior Department of National Parks permission plus CAAT/NBTC registration.
  • Booking: confirmation is by email and WhatsApp after payment, once we have secured your place at the campground. Have your passport number ready for the accident insurance.

Pickup and meeting point

Hotel transfers on both days are included from the main areas of Koh Samui: Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut, Maenam, Choeng Mon, Bang Rak and Plai Laem. Remote areas (Nathon, Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam, Bang Kao, Thong Krut and similar) cost 400 THB per person return. Day-one pickup is 07:30–08:30, with check-in at the pier at 08:30–08:45. We send your exact time and the pier location the day before. Leave big luggage at your hotel and travel with a small bag.
